item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
[+] Some additional thoughts for you
– hide block

I do have to admit, once i finished the writing i read it about fifty times and every time there’s something that felt out of place or unnecessary but I didn’t know how to approach it. ( got scared to trim it.)

IMO: just trim it.

The central core or what i’m really trying to say through the article would be learning who you really are or having peace with you inner conflict and finding power from it. Once the inner peace is achieved no one can really stop you or tell you that your wrong, but the society as a whole always finds a loop hole on the idea. So I guess i didn’t really made it clear.

I think the central problem with the article, in terms of achieving this at the moment, is that this journey to find peace with your inner conflict isn't actually what the story is about? Like, the Foundation swoops in after it happens, so this like, intimate, personal struggle isn't shown; and instead we have this kinda, overview of what happened as a result of it happening?

My suggestion would be to do one of two things: either make this a tale, or start this sooner in the story.

In the first, you'd be radically changing the PoV so it'd be from SCP-XXXX-1's perspective, and entirely centred around them being put in a place where they're forced to find the peace within them, or in a place where finding that peace is their entire struggle, and the story would unfold as they gradually begin to find it while stuff around them gets worse; and the resolution would likely be when the Foundation comes in an interferes or something.

In the second, the focus would be the Foundation locking up -1 just as he's starting to gain this inner power, and so the central conflict would be around this boy trying to achieve the peace he needs whilst the Foundation are doing everything that they can to stop it: the ending would likely be the boy escaping to form the cave and the peaceful area, instead of that being the start. Like pacing would probably look something like "Foundation grabs minor reality bender; reality bender gets stronger; Foundation does stuff to try and stop this; bender keeps getting more powerful; bender escapes and creates a place of peace, as a mirror to the place of conflict that was the foundation for him".

item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

This doesn't have enough 'conflict' driving the story forwards: everyone feels like a passive observer at best, and there's not really anything pulling this forwards. It doesn't help that the various elements feel…disconnected?

Like, the exploration log doesn't smoothly lead into the interview because there's nothing really tying the exploration into the idea of the division between two church groups and that whole conflict; the two things feel completely separate thematically, particularly since the role of the snake and the yurt and stuff is just…completely irrelevant to the interview with -1 and the discovery that there's some spooky churches behind this and there's like…two sets of people and stuff? It feels like this just, doesn't tie all the elements involved in this together well enough, or do much with anything and it's underwhelming as a result.

I would strongly suggest trimming down the concept: figure out what stuff is actually necessary, and get rid of all the unnecessary anomalous stuff. Like, you have this dude who's meant to be able to shape earth but that never actually comes up in this, so cut that aspect. You have the giant snake, but it's not really a major element so cut it from the description. You have the dude manifesting anomalies and talk of this spreading further, but none of that comes up so cut it. Be ruthless: anything that does not serve either the characterisation, the narrative or the emotional response here is unnecessary. Equally: any narrative thread that doesn't go anywhere is unnecessary; any characterisation that isn't purposeful is unnecessary.

This, at it's core, needs a central thing holding it up: an idea, or a theme; and it needs to figure out how to introduce that theme early and expand on it, and explore it throughout. Everything should serve the central core of this: the exploration should introduce it, the interview should expand it, and the note at the end should resolve it.

In it's current state, I would downvote this. I…am not confident that a version of this exists that I would upvote without you effectively starting from scratch on a more streamlined article.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

is to be kept in a standard humanoid cell and itwhich should be suspended in mid-air

with height measuring 300m from the sea level

this phrasing implies exactly 300m; "at least 300m above" would be clearer than "with height measuring 300m from"

It feels to me like measuring it from sea level is a mistake: you want to convey that it's 300m from the ground, which isn't necessarily sea level.

Four wires are to be installed on all four sides to keep the cell stable.

I think the exact details of the suspension can be elided; with the sole exception being if we need to understand this to know how a containment breach or something occurred.

It is to be noted that all carbon-based life areis prohibited to enterfrom entering SCP-XXXX-1’s containment cell.

'carbon-based life' feels clunky here; I feel like 'personnel' is sufficient but?

a containment cell under equivalent containment procedures asto SCP-XXXX-1.

A maximum of five hazmat-protected personnel isare permitted to enter SCP-XXXX at any given time.

Five personnel is plural; so are instead of is.

all on-site personnel isare to evacuate or shelter in place until MTF-Theta-4 ("Gardeners") apprehend SCP-XXXX-1 and its anomalies manifestation.

I think you want 'anomalous manifestations' here?

Description:

I'd get rid of the horizontal line immediately after this; though tbh, I'd generally lean to keeping the description and the first sentence of the description on the same line.

SCP-XXXX consists of two interrelated anomalies: a cave, designated as SCP-XXXX

This is janky: you can't assign 'SCP-XXXX' to both 'the overall' and 'the cave' like this.

the abandoned Mining facility

mining shouldn't be capitalised here or anywhere in sentences like this.

in Tavan Bogd, Mongolia

in the ConProcs, you refer to it as "located in Altai Tavan Bogd, Mongolia"; and it feels like you should be consistent here?

it is measured to be around 6 kilometers deep.

It's unclear whether this refers to the cave or the mine; I'd move the measurement depending on which:

SCP-XXXX is a 6km deep cave under the abandoned mining facility in Tavan Bogd, Mongolia.

or:

SCP-XXXX is a cave under the 6km deep abandoned mining facility in Tavan Bogd, Mongolia.

This also prevents the kinda janky two clauses joined by a comma structure.

at least one kilometer in length, that resides within the cave

this feels really big in relation to the cave depth but? I guess it works if the cave is largely horizontal rather than vertical? It might be worth specifying an area the cave system takes up

Within SCP-XXXX are groups of humanoid entities stationary in place, their physical traits are as same as humans but is made out of a roots that is growing a different species of flowers, those flowers are identical to the organism above the surface and is emitting unknown amount of pollen.

This is a really long run on sentence that really needs to be two sentences at least.

'physical traits' to me implies 'they move like people', I think 'physical appearance' might be what you're aiming for? Or alternatively to just say 'humanoid entities that are stationary and made out of roots'.

'stationary in place' is redundant: one implies the other.

I'm not sure what you mean by 'organism above the surface', unless you mean 'identical to non-anomalous flowers'?

The pollen seemed to affectaffects the mind of a subjects who entered the proximity of the humanoids.

'seemed' is an unnecessary cop out; and the rest is a tense change to make it read better.

When inhaled the pollen

"When the pollen is inhaled,"

It is unknown what will happen after the symptoms as it is yet to be recorded.

This is weird phrasing because it kinda implies the foundation like, were taking notes of someone being affected, and then like…stopped after a while and then didn't note down what else happened.

"The long term effects of exposure are currently unknown." would be a better way to phrase this idea.

Similar to the humanoids, SCP-XXXX has an ecosystem made entirely out of carbon-based life and is being inhabitant by an animals that is identical to animals above the cave, however, the animals are made out of the same components as their surroundings, particularly different species of woods, plants, etc.

This is another huge run on sentence that really needs broken into smaller parts.
'an ecosystem made entirely out of carbon-based life' is unnecessary and can be cut; same for 'similar to the humanoids': just be like 'SCP-XXXX is inhabited by animals composed of plant matter, which are analogous to non-anomalous animals'. Specifying 'woods, plants, etc.' basically conveys nothing.

Footnote 2: It is noted that there’s no soft substance of a human or other animal body, consisting of muscle and fat are present inside of SCP-XXXX.

'It is noted that there's no substance resembling soft tissue, such as muscle and fat, present inside SCP-XXXX'

It is speculated that these animals have grown out of nature and started to inhabit the area, however it is yet to be proven.

I would cut this because it's just, unnecessarily vague. Perhaps saying 'It is speculated that these animals have evolved naturally' would work but?

During substantial viewing of SCP-XXXX, it was apparent that the biome inside of SCP-XXXX is contagious to the outside world.

This is weird; it doesn't work for me at all and I think it's the way the information is being presented. Something like:

The biome within SCP-XXXX is capable of spreading outside the cave system

would be clearer; but it'd raise questions of why the ConProcs don't really have anything to stop the spread beyond 'arrest stuff leaving the cave'.

It's also unclear what you mean by 'biome' since the only life you've referred to so far is plants making up people/animals, whereas this sounds like you're referring to like…plant life?

3 months after SCP-XXXX’s discovery the biome has spread about 7m outside of the cave. Causing the containment of the area to expand along with it.

These should be the same sentence.

Currently, there’s no way of stopping it.

'there is'

Its skin is olive-brown from sun damage and deteriorating, physically it looks as if it in its mid-teens but its age is currently unknown.

This is janky as hell too; something like "Its skin is olive brown from sun damage; physically it appears to be in its mid-teens though the actual age of SCP-XXXX-1 is unknown." might read better but it feels a little like this should perhaps be two sentences?

made entirely out of organic material.

'organic material' is entirely too vague: 'plant matter' would be better if that's what you're aiming for? Otherwise the assumption is 'blood and flesh' and then you just have a normal dragon, y'know?

Entities length is unknown.

I'm not a fan of this sentence or the information it conveys: it feels like something like "The entity is estimated to be [30-50m] long" would be clearer; with the size varied depending on your idea of how big this is.

With indeterminate means, SCP-XXXX-1 can manipulate any carbon-based life for its disposal, this includes causing earthquakes and using it's surroundings as a weapons through telekinesis.

I'd cut the 'With indeterminate means,' here; it feels like it's better to just say what it can do and not specify how.

Footnote 3 is also unnecessary and I'd cut it.

Though it is studied that SCP-XXXX-1, when unresponsive, will still exhibit its anomalous ability and affect the surrounding air, causing asphyxiation on the subject closer to SCP-XXXX-1’s unconscious body.

Consider:

SCP-XXXX-1, when unconscious, will still exhibit anomalous properties which can affect the surrounding air and cause asphyxiation in nearby subjects.

'nearby' feels vague; but I think it's better than specifying it. Though, to be honest, introducing yet more anomalous properties here feels like a mistake: IMO the abilities of -1 need trimmed to one thing it can do.

SCP-XXXX and SCP-XXXX-1 were discovered byduring a series of civilian interviews in Altai Tavan Bogd, Mongolia in █/██/2020

I'd unredact this date fully: the date isn't sensitive information; particularly not more sensitive than what this SCP can do.

deployed in to explore the cave and return with the sample

'with the sample' is still really janky even with a footnote explaining what you mean: I would honestly just say they were deployed to explore the cave and leave it at that.

After they had not returned 24 hours later, a recovery team was dispatched to investigate, only the non-organic components of MTF Zeta-9's equipment were found.

I would probably cut this? Idk, it feels like opening with 'we didn't find Zeta-9' undercuts a lot of the tension of the log because we know it turns out badly?

Maybe it'd work better noted at the end?

Agent Olson: got it.

Missing capital

Agent Olson: Currently… nothing.

It's unclear if Olson means 'We have no ideas about what the cave does' or 'This cave does nothing'

Agent Ouyulan: Then how are we going to travel through this anyway?

There's nothing to indicate there'd be difficulty travelling through this yet.

any of you heard anything?

Shit! why did it get dark? everyone flashlight on!

This is weird cos there's been no indication it got dark before this?

The snake lunges at Agent Ouyulan, but she opens fire on the creature, however it doesn't seemed to be affected.

'but' here implies 'the gun fire prevents the lunge', which the 'however it doesn't seem to be affected' directly contradicts.

During its rampage, its tail hits Agent Olson sendingwhich sends him flying.

The snake is seen swallowing Agent Zachary whole

you need to establish the scale of the snake before this: the implication from 'a snake skeleton' is 'snake sized' whereas 'swallows a man whole' implies 'much larger'.

Well shit, guess we're alone, are we?

Yeah, let us stick together. Don't wander off somewhere else alone. Let's get going.

These are highly trained professionals. Wandering off alone is like…the last thing they should expect the other to do.

The camera activates, the date on the feed tellsindicates its been five hours since the snake attack.

Frantic panting can be heard behind the camera as Agent Olson is seen running through a narrow tunnel,with a bright light can be seen inat the end of it.

The three agents finally reaches a wide space.

'finally' implies the passage of time but cos it's not really shown, it feels weird? Maybe 'After an hour, the three agents reach a wide space' would be better?

found jack shit and now we're in a completely different place.

Agent Olson starts to look around the area, picking up a rock and peddle, feeling the walls of the cave, the camera went static for three minutes and Agent Olson is sitting crossed leg, facing the wall.

Run on sentence

Also I think you mean 'pebble'? But it's weird for Olson to pickup a rock and then not do anything with it: maybe indicate they put it in a sample bag and store it in their rucksack or something?

Is it me or is the air is less timid than when we started?

'timid' is still not the word you're looking for here. I think you want 'thin' maybe?

(a fore)

I think this should really be like 'from off-camera' or something?

drink this, it might help.

It seems like something is messing with frame.

'frame' isn't the right word here: I think maybe 'with the signal' or something but??

No need for messingto mess with that thing

Agent Luna: Umm Cap!

This is the only place anyone is referred to as 'Cap': I would use the more familiar designation.

They all are human.

'human' feels strong here; 'They are all human' would be more grammatically correct but 'They all look like people' might be clearer?

The feet of the crowds embedded into the flower field.

Saying this implies 'the feet are suddenly embedded into…' whereas I think you're really trying to convey that they always were: maybe highlighting someone looking down and noticing it or something would work better?

it seems like these people were on a run?

The description does not imply this to be the case so it feels like a jarring suggestion.

//Agent Olson was silent/

Missing a / at the end

facilities in a three-decade span.

The hyphen is unnecessary too

You caused thousands of deaths.

Hence why you're here.

This isn't actually why -1 is here; -1 is here because he's anomalous and the foundation locks up anomalies; they don't really care about regular humans who kill folk.

SCP-CXXX-1: Will you let me go if I answer? I need to go to my people.

'CXXX' should be 'XXXX'

But I won’t promise you to answer everything.

'But I won't promise I'll answer everything.'

To be honest I can't quite tell you… I never opened it before.

This implies "-1 doesn't know", which it's weird for Kent to follow with 'You can tell me'.

Dr. Kent: Why?

This feels like it should be "How?" as in "How were your peoples existence threatened"

When i was a child, there was a two division of belief, and our people belong in none of those division.

I'm not sure what you mean by 'division of belief'

This whole paragraph feels…very expositional? In like, a bad way: it's just dumping a lot of info in our lap without really giving us a reason to care about the conflict.

first generations to havebe in touch with their inner self.

Did you made them turn them into a tree like your people?

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
► my detailed thoughts◄
- close

SCP-XXXX is to be stored in Containment Area M21 located in 300m underground of the Gobi desert in Mongolia.

Delete that second “in” (right before 300m)

SCP-XXXX is to be held in a 5 m cube made of entirely Tungsten metal, with no gap for organic life to enter.

Why does it matter that the cube be Five meters in length/widtch/height? What if it were 4.98 meters? Would that invalidate the containment? This is why specific measurements of containment chambers is mostly avoided these days.

If any entities that reside in SCP-XXXX-1 move from their position, they are to be immediately apprehended and interrogated before being held in a cell with same containment procedure as SCP-CXXX.

Suggest: Entities residing in SCP-XXXX-1 that move from their position, are to be apprehended, interrogated, and remanded to a containment cell under equivalent containment procedures as SCP-XXXX.

No more than five personnel wearing Hazmat suits, are to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at the same time. Its activity is to be monitored 24/7 and no unauthorized personnel and civilian are to be in the proximity of the area or enter SCP-XXXX-1.

Suggest: A maximum of five hazmat protected personnel are permitted to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at any given time. Access to SCP-XXXX-1 is restricted to security cleared personnel.

In the event of a Containment Breach, all on site researchers and personnel are to evacuate immediately or stay in shelter until the MTF Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) arrive at the facility and apprehended the entity.

Suggest: In the event of a containment breach, all on-site personnel are to evacuate or shelter in place until such time as MTF-Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) apprehend the entity.

ALSO: which entity? Clarify

SCP-CXXX consists of two components: a cave (SCP-XXXX-1) and humanoid protecting it (SCP-XXXX).

Suggest: SCP-XXXX consists of two interrelated anomalies: a cave, designated as SCP-XXXX-1 and a humanoid entity guarding the cave, designated as SCP-XXXX.
ALSO: I suggest reversing the designations, the Cave could be the XXXX and the humanoid, -1, because it seems the cave is the central anomaly.

SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sunburn and wears an old dark green Hun area deel1 which been ripped and torn, however, SCP-XXXX refused to change it.

SCP-XXXX has the ability to manifest entities made out of natural components which resemble a Chinese dragon. Entities length is unknown.
So several things, “an old dark green Hun area deel” is confusing… suggest: “SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sun damage and an deteriorating, dark-green Hun deel that the entity refuses to change.” & I don’t know what “made out of natural components” means in this context, so I would clarify.

ALSO: IS this meant to be two paragraphs? If so, there is no spacing between them.

SCP-XXXX-1 is a cave under abandoned Mining factory, it is measured to be around 6 kilometers deep.

Suggest: a cave under an abandoned mining facility, measured to be approximately six kilometers below the surface.

  • There is no such thing as a mining factory, change this everywhere… it’s a facility or just a mine.

However, how big SCP-XXXX-1 mass is impossible to measure. SCP-XXXX-1 resides a snake-like creature approximately 1 kilometers, maybe even bigger.

Suggest: Exact measurements of SCP-XXXX-1’s dimensions have been impossible due to a large serpentine entity, at least one kilometer in length, that resides within the cave.

About fifty kilometers down, there is a massive field stretching further from the human eye, filled with stationary humanoids varies in ages, they're made out of natural components, different species of flowers but growing in the same root. The radio cuts off the moment entering SCP-XXXX-1.

Fifty kilometers down where? I thought you said the cave was 6 km below the surface? What do you mean? Also this is just really awkwardly written.

The investigation into SCP-XXXX-1 and its relation with SCP-XXXX is ongoing.

Cut this. It’s implied because there’s more to read after it.

Due to the unknown nature of SCP-XXXX, MTF-Zeta-9 (Mole Rats) were deployed in to explore the cave and return with the sample

Suggest: were deployed to explore the cave and return with samples of ___
What samples? Samples of what?

After they had not returned 24 hours later, a recovery team was dispatched to investigate, only the non-organic components of MTF Zeta-9's equipment were found.

Suggest: No updates were received from the MTF, and after twenty-four hours, command mobilized a recovery team. Only the team’s equipment was found, missing any components made with non-synthetic materials.

He continues to cough. His cough becomes more severe as he goes.

Why is this in bold? Every other bit of narration in the log is in italics, not bold.

a can of water

a can of water?

You have so many awkward phrases and poorly structured sentences… I would sit down and really examine your work here, and see if you can't clean it up without myself or another critter to do so.

Additionally, all the dialogue is stilted and hard to read. Go through it and say each line aloud, then if it sounds awkward try to make it sound more grounded and believable.

Overall:

  • There’s a lot of spelling mistakes and failures to capitalize properly in the dialogue.
  • There are lots of exclamation marks in the dialogue. Keep in mind that the “!” implies yelling or very energetic vocalizations…
  • Don’t do the whole date, team, members and label, over and over in the log. BUT you should include a time stamp, as otherwise I don’t know how much time has passed between the breaks.
  • When Olsen starts talking to himself when he’s alone and he doesn’t think command can hear him, it just seems like exposition dump. It doesn’t make sense. People don’t have monologues when they’re by themselves in real life. SO this feels out of place.
  • The second collapsible is an interview with XXXX-1, BUT I thought -1 was the Cave? You consistently switch between -1, -2., and plain XXXX… but that’s confusing because before this second log, there’s no mention of a -2
  • Audio data of Exploration 02, is very strange. It’s the researcher just speaking into his recording device. BUT why not just have him wear a camera and describe it to us in clinical ways? That would be better.
  • Honestly, there’s way too much exposition in this. I would trim this down to 50% of its current length, and tighten up the dialogue.

item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

My biggest issue with this is that a lot of the writing is not good: I'd really advise running this through an automated checker like e.g. libreoffice writer so you can catch easy to find mistakes like the lack of capitalisation etc. I've tried to highlight as much as I can here but I have almost certainly missed stuff cos there's just…a lot.

Beyond this, the jump between the exploration logs and the interview is too big: there's no connective writing between them so it just feels…too sudden? Like in part because -2 doesn't show up in the explorations at all and in part because thre's not really like, any reference to the events of the explorations in it or anything so it's just…there?

The actual exploration logs are fine but they feel…a little directionless? I don't think this is necessarily an issue so much as the slight lack of focus on the interesting events: two people being grabbed by a snake feels like it should be a huge focal event, rather than something which kinda happens in the background, y'know?

It also kinda feels like a lot of this is building up without a clear direction: that might be easier to introduce once you've written more of it, it's hard to tell; but it doesn't feel like all the elements are going to come together in some kind of satisfying conclusion yet.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

The abandoned Mining factory in ██████ ███████, Mongolia

I'd probably name this place: anyone with clearance to see this file almost certainly has clearance to see where it is; otherwise how would they know where to go.

Also this image is ~4MB in size and pretty tiny in the page: I'd recommend opening it in an image editing program and downscaling it (you can ask in #site11 on IRC if you're having difficulty with this)

Item #: SCP-XXXX

I wouldn't necessarily bother including the Item # and Object Class lines at the start if you're using a header that includes them too.

Containment Area M21 is to be located in 300m deep underground ofin the Gobi desert in Mongolia.

I would probably specify that SCP-XXXX-2 is to be stored in this containment area, or at least tie it into the SCP file more.

The 'to be' is technically fine but generally it's advised to say what the Containment Procedures are, rather than should be. 'deep' is to be cut because we can assume that "300m underground" means "down" and it feels clunky here.

SCP-XXXX-2 is to be held in a 5 m cube made of entirely Tungsten metal, the walls are to be (50m) thick on each side, with no gap for planetary or organic life to enter.

My concern with this is that it's a lot of detail that doesn't feel important: the exact size and thickness of the cube aren't really that important; and neither is the exact material it's made of; particularly since none of this detail is referenced later.

Something like:

SCP-XXXX-2 is held in a tungsten cube that cannot be accessed.

Would be clearer and conciser.

The air ventilation of the cell will be 3000 miles (4828.032 kilometers) in length away from the cell and to be checked three times a week.

The foundation always uses metric (so no miles figure) and I would not specify the length to that precision, or indeed, any precision generally? Also like…3000 miles is really far: like, for reference, Tokyo is 1877 miles from Ulaanbaatar and Manila is 2434 miles from Ulaanbaatar.

If any of humanoids that resides in SCP-XXXX-1 are to move from their respective station

'humanoids' feels odd here: I believe the people you are referring to are actually humans? 'respective station' is odd: generally in english, station refers to either 'position in society' or like 'a train station', so 'position' would be better than 'respective station'.

they are to be immediately apprehended and held in the same containment cell as SCP-XXXX and is questioned for further notice.

Do you mean SCP-XXXX-2 here? Also 'questioned for further notice' doesn't make sense; I'd likely used 'interrogated' in place of 'questioned' and I'd probably cut the 'for further notice' completely.

I'd also strongly suggest putting them in a separate containment chamber; and reordering so it's "immediately apprehended and interrogated before being held in the…"

No more than five personnel, wearing in Hazmat suits, are to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at the same time time.

Specifying 'at the same time' prevents the implication that only five people can ever enter.

and no unauthorized personnel and civilian are to be in the proximity of the area or enter SCP-XXXX-1

this can be assumed: they are unauthorized so they are not allowed in.

Unauthorized personnel under level 5 entering the area without permission are given Class C amnestic and is reassigned to a different project. Civilian is to given Class-A amnestic, and is to quarantined based on the severity of their bodily form and psyche.

I'd cut this; we don't need to know how they're punished and we can assume folk who access without permission are to be punished.

In the event of a Containment Breach

"Containment Breach" doesn't need to be capitalised here.

all on sight researchers

'site': 'sight' is 'vision'

or to stay in shelter until the MTF Theta-4 ("Gardeners") are to arrive at the facility and apprehended the entity.

SCP-CXXX consists of two components; a cave (SCP-XXXX-1) and a humanoid protecting it (SCP-XXXX-2).

I would generally avoid defining SCP-XXXX in this way because it forces you to refer to -1 and -2 a lot and means you almost never refer to the whole. In this case, I'd likely define -2 as the base anomaly and leave the cave as -1.

The semi-colon (;) should be a colon here (:) too technically but I think the first change means you don't need to worry about this.

SCP-XXXX-2 resembles a small Hun human male in his mid-teens, standing 169 cm (5,5) and weight around 55 kg (123 lbs).

Again, foundation only uses metric so don't include the imperial conversions here. This said: his exact height and weight aren't important for a reader to understand the anomaly so I'd probably just cut this. I'd also avoid using 'resembles' and other vague words: just say he is a human here even if he's a human with anomalous properties.

Back hair and brown eyes.

This is a sentence fragment (i.e, the issue is it contains no verb: something like "SCP-XXXX-2 has black hair and brown eyes" would be clearer, though if you do cut the height/weight in the last sentence, you could refer to these at the end of the sentence. I'm also assuming 'Back hair' was a typo for 'Black hair'.

Footnote 1: A deel (Mongolian: дээл [deːɮ]; Buryat: дэгэл, [dɛɡɛɮ]) is an item of traditional clothing commonly worn since centuries ago among the Mongols and other nomadic tribes of Central Asia, including various Turkic peoples, and can be made from cotton, silk, wool, or brocade

This isn't a very good description of what a deel is because it entirely focuses on who wears it and what it's made from; whereas if you're putting a footnote in to explain what it is, you want to focus on 'what does it look like'.

It also looks like it's ripped from wikipedia: this is fine but you will have to cite it if so. I recommend checking out the Image Use Policy here since it talks a lot about how to ensure material is compatible with the wiki's license and how to attribute the images; whilst wikipedia words aren't an image, the same policy applies here.

which has been ripped and thronetorn, however, SCP-XXXX-2 refused##greens## to change it.

Instance of SCP-XXXX-2 anomalies properties, are manifestation of Reptilian (Saurosida) entity strongly resembling a dragon made out of natural components.

The start of this is kinda a mess; I'd probably suggest rephrasing to e.g.:

SCP-XXXX-2 has the ability to manifest entities made out of natural components which resemble a dragon

That said: "natural components" is super vague; and it might be worth specifying if this is Chinese style dragons or Western style dragons

Its full length is impossible to measure but is hypothesized to be between 1000 and 2000 kilometers.

"Its" is unclear if you mean "SCP-XXXX-2" or "the entity"; I'd probably use 'unknown' in place of 'impossible to measure' because it seems to me that it'd be easy to measure this theoretically if it stood still. I'd also use 'estimated' in place of 'hypothesized' here.

1000 and 2000 kilometers is also too big. Like…godzilla is maybe 300m tall at most (it varies depending on the film; usually 100m is closer to the average), which means this thing is 5000 godzillas long at minimum and likely 15000 godzilla's long using the average godzilla height)

SCP-XXXX-1 is a Cognitohazardous cave under a destroyed and abandoned Mining factory

neither cognitohazardous nor mining should be capitalised here. I would probably only use one of 'destroyed' and 'abandoned' here since there's a lot of overlap in their meaning. Also 'cognitohazardous' is super broad and you really do have to specify how here; or just…not mention the properties at all.

it is measured to be around 4000 kilometers deep

4000km deep takes you through the crust of the earth (30km thick) and the mantle of the earth (2900 km thick) and into the outer core of the planet.

The deepest mine in the world, currently, is the Mponeng gold mine. It extends about 4km deep, or around 1/1000th of the depth of this mine.

Like I get this is like…anomalous and stuff but it does not feasible for the mine to be this deep without this being a lot more of a big deal than it currently is.

However, how big SCP-XXXX-omega mass is impossible to measure.

what is SCP-XXXX-omega? This is one of the only two places here you mention it and you never define it.

The other place implies they can enter SCP-XXXX-omega which makes measuring it's mass feel weird? So I'd probably cut this but??

SCP-XXXX-1 resides a snake-like creature approximately 200 kilometers, maybe even bigger.

'maybe even bigger' is real casual and I would not include it. Rephrasing to lead with the snake creature would be clearer e.g.: "A snake-like creature approximately 200km long resides in SCP-XXXX". Again though, 200km is really big to the point where if you said 2km, I would say it's probably too big still.

About fifty kilometers down, there is a massive field stretching further from the human eye

'stretching further than the human eye can see' is a good metaphor to grasp for but this is a SCP description: you want to describe things objectively using set sizes rather than vague things like 'larger than can be seen'

filled with stationary humanoids varies in ages, they're made out of natural components, different species of flowers but growing in the same root

this feels…muddled. It probably needs to be a few sentences to make it read right but I'm not exactly sure how best to do that.

Picture of a wooden horse taken during the second exploration

I'd probably move this into the second exploration

The instants of SCP-XXXX-1's anomalous properties became apparent when entering the area.

I'm not sure what you mean by 'instants' here but it feels like this would be better as 'SCP-XXXX-1's anomalous properties become…'

Then again, 'anomalous properties' is the kinda super vague statement I'd generally urge folk to avoid cos it can be basically anything; it'd be more effective to say something like "Radio signals cut off inside SCP-XXXX-1" say.

It is hypnotized that SCP-XXXX-1 refracts of all organic structures, even humans and animals, but it is yet to be backed up.

'hypnotized' should be 'hypothesized'. I'm not sure what you're getting at with 'refracts': maybe like, 'restructures all organic structures' or 'reshapes' or something? 'refracts' is a phenomenon where light changes direction when it enters a partially transparent material and unlikely to be what you're looking for here.

SCP-XXXX was discovered by serious of civilian interviews and gossips in ███████ ████████ after the mass destruction of major mining facilities.

'SCP-XXXX was discovered during the investigation of the destruction of mining facilities in [place name].'

As before, redacting the place name here is a bad idea and you should just name a place here.

It is noted that the SCP-XXXX-2 was already known amongst the locals as a fairy tale hero, with SCP-XXXX-1 mentioned multiple times during the interviews indicating they're might be connected in some way.

'fairy tale hero' feels super casual here; maybe make mention of it appearing in local mythology instead? Also it feels like this needs to setup a firmer connection spatially between the mine and -1 (as in, where is -1 in relation to the mine?) and a firmer connection between -2 and -1.

The investigation into the origins of SCP-XXXX-1 and its relation with SCP-XXXX-2 is ongoing.

Due to the unknown nature of SCP-XXXX-1, MTF-Zeta-9 (Mole Rats) were sendsent in to explore the cave and return with the sample.

'deployed' would be more clinical than 'sent in'; and 'return with the sample' needs additional detail to indicate what kinda samples they're looking for: at the moment it's just…kinda vague.

However they did not return in time, and Recovery team was dispatched to collect the remaining of the team.

This feels like it should be after the first exploration log; rather than spoiling that they don't return immediately before like…getting to the log, y'know? Same goes for the rest of this paragraph.

Something like "After they had not returned 8 hours later, a recovery team was dispatched to investigate" would flow better; with the option of increasing 8 hours or decreasing it depending on how you feel.

They found MTF-Zeta-9 (Mole Rats) team's all none organic materials like guns, vest, and food cans some completely full and other empty.

Something like "Only the non-organic components of MTF Zeta-9's equipment were found." would be clearer; you don't need to specify the mole rats every time just, y'know, to cut down the length.

Date: █/██20██

I wouldn't redact this either; knowing when this happened is important contextualisation for how long the events took to play out etc.

Subject: inside of SCP-XXXX-1

I'd cut this; there's not really a subject so you don't need to say this.

Team Members: Agents Luna, Ouyulan, Zachary, and Sunder.

Agent Olson: Command, we are entering SCP-XXXX-omega.

same comment about -omega not being defined as earlier; I think you're wanting -1 here?

Command: Roger that! stay in touch as long as you can!

I'd avoid using ! as much as possible: the more you use it, the less emphasis it carries. Also it's the end of a sentence, so the 'stay' after the first should be capitalised.

the five agents began to hike down the cave, the light started to dim away.

Capitalised start of sentences, even here.

you and Agent Sunder grew up closerclose to here, right?

Yup the real countryside pumpkin is me.

do you mean 'bumpkin' here? 'country' would read better than 'countryside' too

not sure what you're trying to imply by 'mouth by mouth forum'; perhaps 'it was spread via word of mouth'?

QuiteQuiet, any of you heard anything?

the ground started to shake and small rubble falls on top of Agent Zachary's head! Olson looked up, there was long intervened vines and roots seemingly identical to a snake skeleton.

'rubble' is collective; I think you want like 'a small rock' here? 'intervened' is probably meant to be 'intertwined' or 'tangled'?

TIME: Corrupted

Ending on the time feels kinda janky here; like…why would it be presented here and not earlier? or like, throughout this since this log takes place over an hour or so

At least we have natural light! I reckon the snake attacked us because of our light.

why are none of them questioning why there is natural light deep within a mine

or does the air is less timid than when we eventually hiked down

'or is the air less timid than when we started' would be clearer though…timid is not the word you're looking for here. I'm not sure what the right word is though.

Agent Olson gets up and looks around and breathing in and out slowly.

I'd replace the second and with a comma

The camera pans out to a giant field filled with what seems to be an ecosystem.

…how does the camera pan out? Why did no-one notice it before since this is implied to be right there since it's just…the camera showing it?

than the animal above

'than animals above ground'

There are very big threes

trees?

The light source of this… the place is completely natural, I have no idea where the sun is even shining from the top of us.

How do they know the light source is natural? It seems like they have no idea where the light is coming from here

But the air becoming even timider than the last cave we were in.

…do you mean 'thinner'?

His cough becomes more severe as he goes.

'as he goes' is missing like a 'towards the light' kinda thing where it says where he's going, y'know?

Also this is bolded instead of italicised

Suddenly Olson turned back and saw a hill fill with flowers, he didn't see before

These should be impartial records of what happened: words like 'Suddenly' feel really out of place here; and 'he didn't see before' should be conveyed via what he says rather than the transcript assuming it.

oh fuck, maybe that place is forcing my allergies to kick me in the balls.

This feels weird like the implication is the hill is far away and unlikely to be the source of the coughing? It seems pollen from the nearby plants would be a much more believable explanation here

Once they were at the top of the hill, the camera zoom to an enormous Yurt, behind the Yurt what seemed to be humanoids, stationary.

I again would not refer to the camera doing stuff; generally an MTF will want to keep hands free so this is more…passive body camera recording than active filming, y'know?

Yurt also should not be capitalised here; and this should probably be a few sentences where they like, explicitly walk around the yurt a little or something so they can see the humanoids

But this one… seems incredible (coughs) a saturated.

I'm not sure what you're trying to get at with 'a saturated' here

they're all people!

on a bee made out of natural components sitting on a yellow flower

this phrasing implies there's something special about a bee being made of natural components but bees are y'know, already made of natural components

And yet… this thing hadhas already taken a life.

Why 'a' life? Like, there's four members of his team who have disappeared so far; and like there's room for him to be uncertain about some of them but only in two people pairs so he has to think either 0, 2 or 4 of them are dead

But I want to ask you seriousa series of questions.

Its alright, but we have estimated that your age is about 2000 years.

What led them to this estimate?

It was quitequiet for three minutes.

[-] Line By Line
